acceptanceCriteria.statement: Spine conformance: the ring is ONE shared module under src/worldengine/ that BOTH front-ends import — not a hand-port of the lab's shader into Planet.js. Hand-porting is what one-route-shared-driver-path exists to stop; it would make rings the ninth extraction the lab never imported back, and the plan's own warning is that wiring into the two-route world means paying to migrate a second time.

verifyVia.input: grep the shipped tree for the ring program, and run tests/one-pipeline-fence.test.js
verifyVia.observable: Exactly ONE ring shader source exists in the repo, under src/. Planet.js imports it; world-engine-lab.html imports THE SAME module and calls it. `sin(t * 30.0)` is absent from Planet.js. IMPORT_BACK_DEBT does not grow, and the fence stays green — a ring module the lab does not import back must fail registration 2b by name.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Rings show real gaps where the moons actually put them. A ringed planet whose moon lands a 2:1 or 3:1 resonance inside the annulus renders a visible division there; a planet with no such moon renders none.

verifyVia.input: Generate the 60-system probe corpus and read each ringed planet's rings.physics after moons are generated
verifyVia.observable: Ringed planets carrying a resonance-producing moon report gaps.length > 0 and ringlets.length > 1, and the gap radius matches moonOrbitMult * (1/2)^(2/3) or * (1/3)^(2/3). Today every one of the 33 reports 0 gaps and 1 ringlet, so this AC fails at HEAD.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A ring's colour comes from what it is made of, not from one fixed palette on every planet. An icy ring reads bright cyan-white, a rocky one dark grey, a dusty one brown.

verifyVia.input: Render a ringed planet of each generated composition class and sample the ring's pixels
verifyVia.observable: Mean ring colour differs measurably between an ice-composition and a rock-composition ring, and each matches its COMPOSITION_COLORS entry rather than the planet's rings.color1/color2.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Tilt a ring toward edge-on and its bands fade smoothly to an even tone instead of flickering and crawling.

verifyVia.input: In the running game, frame a ringed planet and sweep the camera elevation from face-on down through the grazing angles, capturing at each step
verifyVia.observable: Radial pixel variance across the annulus falls monotonically toward zero as elevation drops (bands converging on uRingMeanDensity), and frame-to-frame pixel churn under a small camera move does NOT rise as elevation falls. At HEAD both go the other way. SABOTAGE ARM: force the band-limit clamp to 0.0 and confirm the variance stays high and the churn returns — a clamp that is wired but inert must not be able to pass.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Nothing else about the universe moves. Same planets, same moons, same seeds — wiring the gaps must not reorder any random draw.

verifyVia.input: npm run test:body-identity, plus a direct diff of the 60-system corpus before and after
verifyVia.observable: The body-identity instrument's failure set is IDENTICAL to its pre-existing baseline (3 assertions, the other lane's moon-population drift) with no new failures, and every planet's radius/type/moonCount and every moon's orbitRadiusEarth is byte-identical across the change. Only rings.physics.gaps and .ringlets may differ.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Flying to a ringed planet, the rings read as rings — they hold together as one thing across the approach rather than looking like separate effects switching over.

verifyVia.input: Max flies to a ringed planet in the live build and approaches it from several angles
verifyVia.observable: Max's holistic judgment. Never driven or PASSed by an agent; always deferred-to-max.

inputs: src/generation/PhysicsEngine.js generateRingPhysics() — ringlets, gaps, composition, density, colors. Its gap+ringlet derivation is a pure function of already-drawn rngFloat1/rngFloat5 plus the moon list, which is what makes AC-4 achievable.
src/generation/PlanetGenerator.js:561 — calls generateRingPhysics with moons: [] because moons do not exist yet at that point. This is the reason gaps are empty today.
src/generation/StarSystemGenerator.js:591-600 — the seam where a planet's rings AND its finished moon list both exist. Zero-draw re-derivation goes here.

world-engine-lab.html:486-745 — the lab's ring: ringlet/gap loop, RING_COMPOSITION_COLORS, uRingMeanDensity, and the fwidth(ringT) band-limit clamp at :674. This is the implementation being wired, not a reference to reimplement.
src/rendering/objects/RingRenderer.js — the dead multi-band renderer whose shader body the lab resurrected. Its fate (revive as the shared module, or delete) is part of this work.
outputs: docs/FEATURES/one-pipeline-two-frontends-PLAN.md §3 — the F51 row moves from `GAME ❌ R` toward `✅`, and the 4-of-53 headline moves.
docs/FEATURES/mvp-spine-lab-quality-backlog.md QB-14 — gains the measured intra-band-texture finding.
mustStayWorking: Body identity across the corpus — no RNG reordering (this IS AC-4, and it is the dominant risk).
Planet shadow on the ring — the analytic cylinder test, present identically in both programs.
The Bayer dither-discard + posterize envelope (F50) — rings must keep quantising with the body they orbit; POSTERIZE_QUANTUM is wired to the same shared object and must stay so.
setRingGaps(sceneMoons) from main.js:7805 — the live shepherd-moon path; it must not double-count now that resonance gaps are real.

The uniform-inventory ratchets (lab-surface-ratchet, material-parity-list, swap-ledger) — new uniform names will trip them by design and each needs a named justification plus a step6-parity-ledger.md row matching /^[PGRS]-\d\d$/ inside the LEDGER-CH1 region.
Ring tilt from axialTilt (Planet.js:1539-1540) — unchanged by this work.
The world-engine lab itself must keep rendering its ring; it is the source, not a casualty.
